description:
FILED s543l (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24) while writing the #5333 guard row (Pl/t/signals-01.t 'local-sig').  PRE-EXISTING: the base 9fc6583b (MAIN-READY-110's code) answers the same; not related to `local %SIG` (an element `local $SIG{HUP}` and a plain store show it).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | ./runpcl on 9fc6583b and on the s543l tree):
    $| = 1;
    for my $s (qw(HUP INT TERM ALRM USR1 WINCH)) {
      my $r = eval { local $SIG{$s} = sub { die "died-$s\n" }; kill $s => $$; select(undef, undef, undef, 0.2); "survived" };
      print "$s: ", ($r // "caught $@"); print "\n" if $r;
    }
  perl: every line "SIG: caught died-SIG"
  PCL:  HUP / INT / TERM / ALRM / WINCH "survived" (the die is LOST: the handler RAN -- a print before the die appears --
        and the program goes on after the kill as if it had returned); USR1 "caught died-USR1" (right).
  Also `$SIG{HUP} = sub { die "d5\n" }; eval { kill HUP => $$; ...; 1 }` and a kill with no select after it.

WHAT IT IS (suspect, not measured): the signals SBCL DEFERS run the Lisp handler DIRECTLY (%p-sig-direct-handler ->
%p-sig-deliver, the "DELIVERY" note above +p-sig-taken-over+ in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp); USR1 goes through the relay
thread and sb-thread:interrupt-thread and its die unwinds into the program.  The direct route's non-local exit is
apparently absorbed (a handler-case / without-interrupts around the deferred handler, or SBCL's own deferral
machinery catching the unwind).  `alarm N; sleep M` with a dying handler is RIGHT (signals-01.t row 'alarm-sleep':
sleep's wakeup path).  THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT: put a (format *error-output* ...) in %p-sig-deliver's
:handler arm after the funcall and in a handler-bind around it -- does the p-die-error condition reach it, and who
catches it (sb-unix::%unblock-deferrable-signals / with-interrupts)?

WHY IT MATTERS: the `alarm` + `die` timeout idiom with a self-kill, and every SIGHUP / SIGTERM handler that dies to
leave a loop (a daemon's reload / shutdown), silently continue instead.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a `die` inside a %SIG handler for a signal SBCL runs DIRECTLY (HUP INT TERM ALRM WINCH, self-kill) is LOST -- the program goes on after the kill; perl unwinds to the enclosing eval (USR1, relayed, is right)
triage_reason: a die in a %SIG handler of a deferred signal is lost
